hints.title: Subarray Boundary Obstacle
hints.text: Evaluating every possible start and end index requires quadratic time, which fails on an array of one hundred thousand numbers. If an accumulated running segment becomes negative, why does continuing to extend it harm rather than help any subsequent positive numbers?

hints.title: Tracking Local and Global Maximums
hints.text: Track the maximum subarray sum ending at the current element alongside the overall best subarray sum found so far, resetting the running sum whenever it falls below zero.

hints.title: Linear Kadane Transition
hints.text: Initialize both current maximum and global maximum to the first element. Iterate through the remaining numbers. For each number x, update current maximum to either x alone or x plus current maximum, whichever is larger, then update the global maximum if current maximum exceeds it.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single linear pass tracking running maximum with constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every contiguous subarray (i, j) takes O(N^2) time. For N = 10^5, this requires ~5 * 10^9 operations, exceeding the ~10^8 per-second CPU budget by a factor of 50 and causing Time Limit Exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) auxiliary space suffices because Kadane's algorithm only depends on the previous prefix sum (current_sum = max(num, current_sum + num)), requiring zero extra memory beyond two scalar registers.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling all-negative input arrays correctly (returning the single maximum negative value rather than 0), recognizing Kadane's greedy/DP invariant, and understanding the divide-and-conquer O(N log N) alternative.
